title: An array<array-key, int> argument cannot satisfy a parameter declared array<string, int>

ground_truth.statement: An array key is an int or a string and nothing else, and array-key is int|string, so an array declared array<array-key, int> is an array<int|string, int> and may contain int keys - the argument here contains the int key 0. The callee declares array<string, int> and applies strtoupper() to every key, which under strict_types fails with a TypeError on that int key. Passing an argument of type array<array-key, int> into a parameter of type array<string, int> is therefore unsound: the declared key type is a contract the argument cannot meet, and a diagnostic belongs on the call. PHP also normalises a numeric string key to int, so the caller cannot satisfy a string key type by spelling key 0 as '0' either.

phpstan.reason: PHPStan explicitly defines array-key as a permissive benevolent union rather than a strictly checked int|string alias. ArrayType normalizes that key to implicit mixed, and this baseline level-9 configuration leaves checkImplicitMixed disabled. Silence is therefore an excluded documented configuration-scope difference. An independent check with checkImplicitMixed: true emits argument.type on the unchanged fixture; the rule is implemented.

notes: This tests the array key contract, distinct from the element value contract. The runtime consequence remains real: an int key reaches strtoupper() under strict_types and throws. Psalm 6.20.0 and Mago 1.57.0 diagnose the call. The initial factory report counted PHPStan's level-9 silence as FN, but a later source and documentation audit corrected that classification without changing the fixture or its runtime result. PHPStan's configuration reference explicitly documents array-key as a benevolent union with deliberately lenient checking. In the pinned source, TypeNodeResolver.php:283-284 constructs that union; ArrayType.php:75-82 normalizes it to implicit mixed. The baseline checkImplicitMixed:false then deliberately accepts the key. An independent unchanged-source probe with checkImplicitMixed:true emits argument.type; an explicit int|string spelling also diagnoses. This is a documented dialect/configuration difference, not a missing implemented check, and is excluded consistently with the optional PHPDoc signature check. The older immutable factory reports retain the original FN for audit history; use the corrected cohort report for current claims. The Psalm candidate is a lead only: its suppressed upstream coercion is not the oracle for any tool.

sources.note: lead only; the explicit int key type on the argument side is the part that is kept, the rule was re-derived from the runtime
array-key deliberately resolves to a BenevolentUnionType, not a plain int|string union
the benevolent int|string key normalizes to implicit mixed; StrictMixedType becomes a checked plain union

transformCommonType / transformMixedType map a mixed type to StrictMixedType only when checkExplicitMixed (explicit mixed) or checkImplicitMixed (implicit mixed) is on; with both off the type is returned unchanged and an unspecified key stays lenient, which is why the level-9 run is silent here
line 73 sets checkImplicitMixed: false in the default configuration; conf/config.level10.neon line 5 sets it true, and conf/config.levelmax.neon includes config.level10.neon
